items.title: How tourists and plastic transformed Bali into an 'Island of Trash'
items.description: Known to many as the Island of the Gods, residents fear Bali may soon become the "Island of Trash" due to a deluge of tourists, a lack of rubbish education and the partial closure of a much-needed landfill facility.

items.title: Australian accused of Thai teen's murder tells her family 'I feel bad'
items.description: An Australian man charged with the murder of a 17-year-old girl in Thailand tells her family her death was "out of my control".

items.title: Treasurer promises to 'fix' property tax oversight, but won't say how exactly
items.description: The Treasurer is promising to "fix" an unintended consequence of the government's overhaul of property tax breaks to protect widows and divorcees — but he has refused to say exactly how.

items.title: Hanson spawned the silliest semantic beard-stroking in 20 years
items.description: We've come a long way since it was Pauline Hanson who didn't know the meaning of big words.

items.title: Bahrain and Kuwait targeted in Iran strikes as Hormuz tensions spike
items.description: It comes after the United States says it launched fresh strikes on Iranian military infrastructure near the Strait of Hormuz "in direct response to continued Iranian aggression against commercial shipping".

items.title: Live: No Messi, no problem as Argentine star scores belter
items.description: Messi does not start for Argentina, as Colombia is denied a late winner by the barest of margins and England locks up top spot in Group L. Follow live.

items.title: Trump's Vance jokes fuel succession speculation
items.description: At times, Donald Trump appears to be harking back to his days hosting reality TV show The Apprentice as he leans into speculation about who he will anoint as his successor.

items.title: Venezuela earthquake death toll passes 1,400 as survival window narrows
items.description: The death toll from two earthquakes in Venezuela has climbed beyond 1,400, as searches for survivors intensify during the remaining hours of the window for survival.

items.title: Brisbane man makes fastest human-powered Everest ascent from sea level
items.description: Avalanches, altitude sickness, orcs and Justin Bieber — a Brisbane mountaineer is believed to have set a new world record on Mount Everest for charity, despite every obstacle thrown his way.

items.title: The covert narcissist: Charming on the surface, destructive beneath
items.description: As "narcissist" becomes the catch-all insult of the social media age, here is the crucial difference between everyday selfishness and a serious personality disorder.

items.title: 'Worst' wind lull pushes green poster child South Australia to its power limits
items.description: South Australia is at the bleeding edge of the energy transition but record low winds have pushed its grid to the brink of its limits.

items.title: Murder trial mementos: The Chamberlain artefacts too sensitive to exhibit
items.description: Forty years ago, the chance discovery of a bloodied matinee jacket unravelled a murder conviction. Now, that evidence lives inside a national museum's collection that's too sensitive for public display.

items.title: Shark-spotting drones to monitor 70 NSW beaches every day of the year
items.description: Shark-spotting drones will provide year-round coverage at about 70 beaches along the NSW coast as part of an expanded surveillance program announced after a Sydney mother was attacked by a suspected white shark.

items.title: Karl Stefanovic's 'weird personality' might score him a Logie
items.description: Karl Stefanovic is no longer part of the Nine family but his audience may not be ready to abandon their prodigal son.

items.title: Keith Urban is a country megastar — so why release a yacht rock album?
items.description: Keith Urban explains why he made a yacht rock album and how his Brisbane cover band days shaped Flow State.

items.title: Love story: Holding onto the glimmers of my dad, Blues legend Steve Mortimer
items.description: Erin Mortimer's dad, Bulldogs and Blues legend Steve Mortimer, was diagnosed with dementia at just 60 after years of concussions during his playing career. Erin is holding on to the special memories, and the glimmers of him that remain.

items.title: Guy Montgomery is back with your weekly spelling bee fix
items.description: Feel free to exhale that breath you've been holding in — it's Sunday and that means it's time to get spelling again.

items.title: How many products in your daily life are made from fossil fuels?
items.description: Coal, oil and gas are major ingredients for far more than just energy. Why are we so reliant on oil, and how difficult would it be to find other resources?

items.title: Labor unveils new powers to strengthen social media ban
items.description: Six months into Australia's world-first social media ban for under-16s, the federal government has announced tougher laws that it says will hold big tech to account and keep kids safe online.

items.title: Singha beer dynasty being torn apart by 'ungrateful child' law
items.description: The billionaire family behind the Singha beer company is being torn apart by explosive allegations of assault and a century-old law that protects parents from neglectful children.

items.title: 'Very thankful': Mum of child with amputation grateful for community support
items.description: Braxton's mum says there needs to be more clothing options available for children with amputations, after struggling to find some for her son whose leg became amputated in the womb.

items.title: Key bird observatory shut for months before avian flu detection
items.description: Volunteers and wildlife advocates push to reopen the Eyre Bird Observatory, arguing the station will be critical in monitoring the potential impact of avian flu.

items.title: WA shearing teams look for new ways to make ends meet
items.description: Almost 100 shearing shed workers across regional WA sign up to a new training program aimed at helping contractors and their teams find work beyond the shearing industry.

items.title: Footy's quiet crisis claims its youngest victim
items.description: A talent and a team player, Nick Lowden excelled at Aussie Rules. But the knocks, bumps, hits and collisions were adding up.

items.title: The outback town with no traffic lights attracting city professionals
items.description: After escaping the big smoke, these five young people have swapped the metro rat race for a slower life in the outback – and say they wouldn’t change a thing.
